creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Closing a pane by hand put an error on its row five seconds later:

> The pane local/p21ep311we lost the connection carrying it and has not got one back
> within 5s. [...] Check that the machine holding it is reachable - the run log says
> `tunnel.down` when the connection is the reason, and Muster keeps trying.

Nothing was unreachable. The pane was on `local`, the daemon was healthy, and the pane
closed exactly as asked - it is gone from `muster window` now. The run log has the whole
thing inside two seconds:

```
intent.submitted  ClosePane { pane: "p21ep311we" }  refused: "timed out"
bridge.ended      ending "lost"  reason "terminal attach ended: terminal term_65aca... not found"
```

## Why the ending is wrong

`bridge_report::ending()` matches herdr's closing prose against two phrases - `taken over`
and `already has an attached client` - and everything else falls to `Lost`. The comment
there argues `Lost` is the safe way to be wrong: its answer is to start another bridge,
and being wrong the other way would leave a pane dark on a daemon that is perfectly
healthy.

That holds for a pane that still exists. It does not hold for `terminal ... not found`,
which is the daemon saying the pane is gone. The answer to that is to drop it. Instead the
respawn policy spends attempts dialing a terminal nothing can ever attach to. `Ending`
has no case that means gone - `Lost`, `Refused` and `TakenOver` all describe a pane that
is still there.

## Why it reaches the user

Two readers of `Lost` are both wrong about a closed pane:

- `respawn` treats it as a connection that may come back, and starts up to `LIMIT` replacements.
- `typeable::detail()`'s `Lost` branch is written for a dropped VPN: it names the machine,
  points at `tunnel.down`, and on 0.5.0 also advised closing the pane and opening it again
  - which `12a108b` has since replaced for separate reasons.

So closing a pane produces an error accusing the network. This is the attention surface
Muster exists for, and a false alarm on it is more expensive than a wrong log line.

## What is not settled

How the message outlived the pane. `Waiting::closed` is called from `prune` when the
mirror stops holding a pane, which should have taken this wait with it, and
`Waiting::reconcile` filters on what the view is drawing - the view dropped the pane 11ms
after the bridge ended. Neither prevented the message five seconds later. The
`mirror.resnapshot` at that moment reported `changes: 0`, so the mirror may still have
been holding the pane when `prune` looked, but nobody has traced it.

Also unsettled: whether the respawns actually ran here, and what they cost. Nothing
records a respawn decision.

## Noticed alongside

`raise_problem` and `clear_problem` write nothing to the run log, so the sentence a person
actually read is the one thing the timeline does not contain. Reconstructing this needed
the surrounding events and a guess. Against "every run explains itself" that looks like
its own card.

## Related

`a_2L1AEIpIY` is the other half of the same incident, and neither fix hides the other:
`pane.close` overran the 500ms `HerdrClient::DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` and was reported as refused
though the daemon had already done it. That card is about a timeout read as a failure;
this one is about the bridge death that follows being read as a network problem.
title: 🪦 A closed pane's bridge reads as a lost connection, so a healthy machine is accused
